heading: Publication

calibration.note: Same inherited rhgrh100 calibration; no new measurement was made for this problem. The rules are restated for a three-part problem: two divisibility conclusions from one subgroup construction, and one explicit counterexample.

rules.rule: No sentence may be commentary only. A reason for a step may appear only as a clause of the sentence that takes the step.
No restatement of the claim before the derivation; the proof opens with its first step, and the statement is carried by the closing sentence.
The subgroup-of-Z fact and Lagrange are invoked in one sentence each that says what they consume and what they return; the pigeonhole pairing is a clause of the sentence that uses it.
At most 168 words; aim for 120 or fewer.
Every mandatory node of the content plan is realized or merged with an honest quote; every dependency between nodes in the alignment is still visible in the prose.
rules.from: programme gate for P3 and P4

finite-index-is-the-only-source.reason: A paper uses the finite-index hypothesis where it is needed and does not discuss what fails without it.

positive-exponent-origin.reason: The pigeonhole pairing is written out as the clause that produces the positive exponent (PR3).

normality-to-divisibility.reason: The quotient sentence names the order of the coset and Lagrange, which is this question's answer (PR3).

why-the-set-T.reason: The opening sentence names T as the preimage under the powers homomorphism, the packaging the question asks about.

why-not-a-three-cycle.reason: A paper gives the working counterexample and does not discuss candidates that would not have worked.
